slides.title: Paracetamol
slides.subtitle: Acetaminophen
slides.highlight: Hepatotoxicity risk; count all routes toward daily max; caution in G6PD & renal failure.
slides.moa: Inhibits central prostaglandin synthesis to relieve pain and fever without peripheral anti-inflammatory activity.
doses: Term neonate & child: 10–15 mg/kg/dose PO/PR 4–6 hrly; max 75 mg/kg/day (5 doses/day; child max 4 g/day)
Child 2–12 yr IV: 60 mg/kg/day ÷ 6 hrly or 75 mg/kg/day ÷ 4 hrly; max 75 mg/kg/day (3.75 g <50 kg; 4 g ≥50 kg)
Neonate/infant IV: 30–40 mg/kg/day (<32 wk), 50 mg/kg/day (≥32 wk, ≤28 d), 60 mg/kg/day (29 d–<2 yr) ÷ 6 hrly
PDA closure: 60 mg/kg/day IV/PO ÷ 6 hrly for 3 days (up to 7 days or repeat 3-day course)

caption:
The most prescribed drug in the paediatric ward—yet still easy to overdose if you forget to count every route! 💊

For NEET-PG & ward rounds, remember three key points: Paracetamol lacks anti-inflammatory activity, neonatal IV max doses depend on gestational and postnatal age, and it is used for PDA closure when NSAIDs fail or are contraindicated. Watch for hepatotoxicity with CYP2E1 inducers and never exceed 5 PO/PR doses in 24 hours.
